raw_case_text: Patient A; This is a 40-year-old male patient who came with a non-productive cough for one month and a three-month history of unquantified but significant weight loss. He also had a history of losing his appetite. On initial presentation, he appeared to be chronically ill, and all of his vital signs were within normal limits. The man weighed 52 kilograms and stood 1.74 meters tall, with a BMI of 17.2 kilograms per square meter, indicating that he was underweight. The lymphoglandular system revealed 3 by 4 cm enlarged masses that were mobile, had no overlying skin color change, and were tender in the cervical areas bilaterally, as well as 2 by 3 cm enlarged masses that were soft in consistency, mobile, had no overlying skin color change, and were non-tender on the submental areas. Other findings in the abdomen were a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant, about 5 cm below the right costal border, indicating hepatomegaly, and a soft mass along the line of spleen expansion, suggesting splenomegaly. He was then probed for a possible TB diagnosis, despite the fact that all of the standard TB diagnostic tests were negative. However, as shown below, the abdominal ultrasonography and FNAC (fine needle aspiration cytology) both supported the tuberculosis diagnosis. Abdominal ultrasonography revealed calcified and hypoechoic micronodules in the liver and spleen, as well as numerous enlarged centrally necrotic intra-abdominal lymphadenopathies, indicating disseminated tuberculosis (likely resolving). A FNAC biopsy revealed bilateral cervical and submental lymphadenopathies, with a tuberculous abscess as the most likely diagnosis. He was then tested for retrovirus infection and was found to be positive. The CD4 cell count was 14 cells per millimeter squared. He was offered urine LAM for tuberculosis diagnosis, and the result was positive for TB LAM. He began antiTB treatment, and on the tenth day of treatment, he was started on highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) with Tenofovir+Lamivudine+Dolutegravir (TLD) as per the recommendation. He is now on his 7th month and is apparently healthy, and taking his medication regularly. His weight also increased to 63 kilograms, with a BMI of 20.8, which is normal. The viral load was done 2 weeks back, and it was 800 copies, which is below the threshold for viral transmission (greater than 1000 copies).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old male presented with a non-productive cough of one month's duration, accompanied by anorexia and significant weight loss over three months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 40-year-old male presented with a 1-month history of dry cough, anorexia, and progressive significant weight loss over 3 months. Initial standard outpatient evaluations had been inconclusive.
subjective.past_medical_history: Denies prior chronic illnesses, hospitalizations, or known TB contacts. HIV diagnosed during present hospitalization. Home medications and allergies not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports non-productive cough, anorexia, weight loss; denies fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Chronically ill appearance; vital signs within normal limits. Weight 52 kg, height 1.74 m, BMI 17.2 kg/m^2. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy (3 x 4 cm mobile, tender masses) and submental lymphadenopathy (2 x 3 cm soft, mobile, non-tender masses). Abdominal exam: hepatomegaly palpable 5 cm below right costal margin, palpable splenomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: HIV rapid test: positive; CD4 count: 14 cells/mm^3; initial standard sputum microscopy: negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal ultrasound: calcified and hypoechoic micronodules in liver and spleen, along with numerous enlarged centrally necrotic intra-abdominal lymph nodes. FNAC of cervical and submental lymph nodes: cytomorphology consistent with necrotic tuberculous abscess.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis (cervical/submental lymphadenitis, splenic and hepatic micronodules, necrotic intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy) in newly diagnosed advanced HIV infection (CD4 14 cells/mm^3).
Confirmation: Urine lipoarabinomannan (LAM) test was positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis; FNAC of cervical and submental lymph nodes confirmed tuberculous abscess; abdominal ultrasound revealed disseminated hepato-splenic micronodules and necrotic retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
Differentials ruled out: Lymphoma, Kaposi sarcoma, disseminated histoplasmosis/cryptococcosis.
Treatment & Outcome: Anti-tuberculosis therapy initiated; on day 10 of ATT, highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) was started with tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir (TLD). At 7-month follow-up, patient was clinically well, weight increased to 63 kg (BMI 20.8 kg/m^2), and HIV viral load was suppressed to 800 copies/mL.
